angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 548,907 km at 64.00 pc = 0.11 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 15.6253 +/- 0.0105 mas (same row, RUWE 0.90): 64.00 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.789 +/- 0.0064 solar radii from Bonomo et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of Kepler-37 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..33B/abstract): 548,907 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.79 +/- 0.033 solar masses from Bonomo et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of Kepler-37 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..33B/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5357 +/- 68 K from Bonomo et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Kepler-37 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..33B/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Bonomo et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Kepler-37 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..33B/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/kepler-37.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.542, rounded to two decimals
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of Kepler-37 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] -0.25 dex, from Fulton & Petigura 2018 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....156..264F/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of Kepler-37 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.32187, from Gajdoš et al. 2019 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019RAA....19...41G/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of Kepler-37 (pscomppars): age 3.8 Gyr, from Morton et al. 2016 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJ...822...86M/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: VizieR J/A+A/678/A24/tablec1 (New rotation periods of 67163 Kepler stars), column ProtFin: 26.01 d, the row 0.3 arcsec from the star's J2000 place. The middle of 12 catalogued periods, 9 of them within 20% of it
